claim: Pik-1 and Pik-2 form a linked gene pair arranged in an inverted configuration on chromosome 11 with only ~2.5 kb separating their start codons.
source: The rice NLRs Pik-1 and Pik-2 form a linked gene pair arranged in an inverted configuration on chromosome 11 with only ~2.5 kb separating their start codons (Ashikawa et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Ashikawa et al., 2008, which provides the genomic organization data.

claim: The Pik pair is present in the genetic pool of rice cultivars as two major haplotypes.
source: The Pik pair is present in the genetic pool of rice cultivars as two major haplotypes (Białas et al., 2021; Kanzaki et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Białas et al., 2021 and Kanzaki et al., 2012.

claim: Pik pairs belonging to the K haplotype confer resistance to strains of the rice blast fungus, Magnaporthe oryzae, that harbour the effector AVR-Pik.
source: Pik pairs belonging to the K haplotype confer resistance to strains of the rice blast fungus, Magnaporthe oryzae, that harbour the effector AVR-Pik (Ashikawa et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Ashikawa et al., 2008.

claim: The sensor NLR Pik-1 binds AVR-Pik effectors through a heavy metal-associated (HMA) domain integrated into its architecture.
source: The sensor NLR Pik-1 binds AVR-Pik effectors through a heavy metal-associated (HMA) domain integrated into its architecture (De la Concepcion et al., 2018; Kanzaki et al., 2012; Maqbool et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to De la Concepcion et al., 2018, Kanzaki et al., 2012, and Maqbool et al., 2015.

claim: Upon effector recognition, Pik-1 cooperates with the helper NLR Pik-2 to activate immune signalling that leads to pathogen resistance.
source: Upon effector recognition, Pik-1 cooperates with the helper NLR Pik-2 to activate immune signalling (Zdrzałek et al., 2020) that leads to pathogen resistance.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zdrzałek et al., 2020.

claim: The intensity of cell death was lower when Pikm-1 was co-expressed with Pikp-2 instead of Pikm-2.
source: However, the intensity of cell death was lower when Pikm-1 was co-expressed with Pikp-2 instead of Pikm-2 (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1 and its supplements, demonstrating differential cell death responses.

claim: Protein accumulation of both Pikp-2 and Pikm-2 proteins in planta was similar.
source: Protein accumulation of both Pikp-2 and Pikm-2 proteins in planta was similar (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Pikm-2 is required for the full Pikm-mediated cell death response to the AVR-Pik effectors in N. benthamiana.
source: These results indicate that Pikm-2 is required for the full Pikm-mediated cell death response to the AVR-Pik effectors in N. benthamiana.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental results showing reduced cell death when Pikm-1 is paired with Pikp-2 instead of Pikm-2.

claim: A single amino acid change at position 230 was responsible for the major differences in cell death responses.
source: A single amino acid change at position 230 was responsible for the major differences in cell death responses (Figure 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by mutagenesis experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: The Asp230Glu mutation in Pikp-2 showed an increase in the level of cell death response to AVR-Pik effectors.
source: Despite the similar properties of their side chains, the Asp230Glu mutation in Pikp-2 showed an increase in the level of cell death response to AVR-Pik effectors (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 2A and supplements.

claim: The Glu230Asp mutation in Pikm-2 reduced the cell death response to each AVR-Pik effector compared with wild-type Pikm-2.
source: By contrast, the Glu230Asp mutation in Pikm-2 reduced the cell death response to each AVR-Pik effector compared with wild-type Pikm-2, displaying only a slight response to AVR-PikD (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 2B and supplements.

claim: Pikm-2 Glu230 residue is involved in the extended response to AVR-Pik effectors observed in Pikm.
source: This points to a major involvement of the Pikm-2 Glu230 residue in the extended response to AVR-Pik effectors observed in Pikm (De la Concepcion et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the mutagenesis data and supported by a citation to De la Concepcion et al., 2018.

claim: When Pikp-1 was co-expressed together with Pikm-2, it led to cell death response in the absence of AVR-PikD.
source: However, we noticed that when Pikp-1 was co-expressed together with Pikm-2, it led to cell death response in the absence of AVR-PikD (Figure 3, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 3.

claim: No NLR autoactivation was observed in the reciprocal mismatched pair Pikm-1/Pikp-2.
source: We did not observe NLR autoactivation in the reciprocal mismatched pair Pikm-1/Pikp-2 (Figure 3, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 3.

claim: A Lys217Arg mutation in the P-loop motif of Pikp-2 abrogates Pik-mediated cell death responses to AVR-PikD in N. benthamiana.
source: A Lys217Arg mutation in the P-loop motif of Pikp-2 abrogates Pik-mediated cell death responses to AVR-PikD in N. benthamiana (Zdrzałek et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zdrzałek et al., 2020.

claim: Introducing the Lys217Arg mutation in Pikm-2 abolished Pikm-mediated cell death response to the rice blast effector AVR-PikD.
source: Introducing this mutation in Pikm-2 abolished Pikm-mediated cell death response to the rice blast effector AVR-PikD (Figure 4, Figure 4—source data 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The Lys217Arg mutation in Pikm-2 abrogated the constitutive cell death response triggered by the Pikp-1/Pikm-2 NLR mismatch.
source: Introducing this mutation in Pikm-2 abolished Pikm-mediated cell death response to the rice blast effector AVR-PikD (Figure 4, Figure 4—source data 1) and also abrogated the constitutive cell death response triggered by the Pikp-1/Pikm-2 NLR mismatch (Figure 4, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Introducing Asp559Val in the MHD motif of Pikp-2 abolished cell death responses to AVR-PikD.
source: Contrary to other NLRs, introducing Asp559Val in the MHD motif of Pikp-2 abolished cell death responses to AVR-PikD (Zdrzałek et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zdrzałek et al., 2020.

claim: The Asp559Val mutation in Pikm-2 abrogated cell death in autoimmune combinations.
source: Consequently, we introduced the equivalent mutation in Pikm-2 and verified that it also abrogated cell death in autoimmune combinations (Figure 4, Figure 4—source data 2)
evidence: The claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Pikm-2 requires an intact MHD motif to trigger cell death.
source: Consequently, we introduced the equivalent mutation in Pikm-2 and verified that it also abrogated cell death in autoimmune combinations (Figure 4, Figure 4—source data 2), confirming that Pikm-2 requires an intact MHD motif to trigger cell death
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental results showing that MHD motif mutation abolishes cell death.

claim: The Asp230Glu mutation in Pikp-2 conferred a strong cell death response in the absence of the effector when co-expressed with Pikp-1.
source: The Asp230Glu mutation in Pikp-2 conferred a strong cell death response in the absence of the effector when co-expressed with Pikp-1, while only residual constitutive activation could also be observed with Pikm-1 (Figure 5, Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The Glu230Asp mutation in Pikm-2 abrogated constitutive cell death in the presence of Pikp-1.
source: By contrast, the reciprocal mutation at the equivalent position in Pikm-2 abrogated constitutive cell death in the presence of Pikp-1 and reduced the cell death response mediated by AVR-PikD recognition (Figure 5, Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Constitutive cell death triggered by Pik-2 Asp230Glu is dependent on the P-loop and MHD motifs.
source: Additionally, we confirmed that constitutive cell death triggered by Pik-2 Asp230Glu is also dependent on the P-loop and MHD motifs, confirming that this mutation leads to immune activation (Figure 5—figure supplement 2, Figure 5—figure supplement 2—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Cell death responses were reduced but not completely abolished when Pikm-2 or Pikp-2 Asp230Glu were co-expressed with a P-loop mutant of Pikp-1.
source: Interestingly, cell death responses were reduced but not completely abolished when Pikm-2 or Pikp-2 Asp230Glu were co-expressed with a P-loop mutant of Pikp-1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3, Figure 5—figure supplement 3—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: A Gly residue encoded by GGT is an ancestral state at position 230 in Pik-2 and is still present in most Pik-2 sequences from wild Oryza species.
source: This analysis revealed that a Gly residue encoded by GGT is an ancestral state at this position and is still present in most Pik-2 sequences from wild Oryza species (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: A transition from GGT (coding for Gly) to GAT (coding for Asp) in position 230 occurred before the split of Oryza sativa and Oryza punctata.
source: A transition from GGT (coding for Gly) to GAT (coding for Asp) in position 230 occurred before the split of Oryza sativa and Oryza punctata and has been maintained in Pik-2 NLRs of modern rice varieties clustering in the Pikp cultivar K60 (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: A non-synonymous Asp to Glu mutation by a GAT to GAA transversion occurred in the rise of the clade containing the Pikm cultivar Tsuyuake.
source: This change opened the possibility of a non-synonymous Asp to Glu mutation by a GAT to GAA transversion, which occurred in the rise of the clade containing the Pikm cultivar Tsuyuake.
evidence: The claim is inferred from phylogenetic analysis and ancestral state reconstruction.

claim: The Glu230Gly mutation in Pikm-2 abolished the constitutive cell death triggered by Pikm-2 when co-expressed with Pikp-1 in the absence of the effector.
source: The Glu230Gly mutation abolished the constitutive cell death triggered by Pikm-2 when co-expressed with Pikp-1 in the absence of the effector (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Protein accumulation of Pik-1 and Pik-2 alleles was consistently increased when they were expressed together compared to co-expression with empty vector.
source: After co-expression of both Pikp-1 and Pikm-1 alleles in N. benthamiana in combination with the helper Pikp-2 or Pikm-2 alleles followed by western blot, we observed that protein accumulation of Pik-1 and Pik-2 alleles was consistently increased when they were expressed together compared to co-expression with empty vector (Figure 7A).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Pik-1 and Pik-2 associate in sensor/helper NLR heterocomplexes, stabilizing both proteins.
source: This is consistent with a model where Pik-1 and Pik-2 associate in sensor/helper NLR heterocomplexes, stabilizing both proteins (Zdrzałek et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is inferred from protein accumulation data and supported by a citation to Zdrzałek et al., 2020.

claim: Accumulation of the helper Pik-2 in the autoimmune pair Pikp-1/Pikm-2 was consistently higher.
source: Interestingly, accumulation of the helper Pik-2 in the autoimmune pair Pikp-1/Pikm-2 was consistently higher (Figure 7A).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Both Pikp-2 and Pikm-2 could be detected after immunoprecipitation of either Pikp-1 or Pikm-1 sensor NLRs.
source: Both Pikp-2 and Pikm-2 could be detected after immunoprecipitation of either Pikp-1 or Pikm-1 sensor NLRs (Figure 7B).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: None of the Pik-2 mutations generated seem to have a measurable effect on the sensor/helper association.
source: Additionally, none of the Pik-2 mutations generated above seem to have a measurable effect on the sensor/helper association (Figure 7—figure supplement 1, Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 7 supplements.

claim: Mutations in the P-loop and MHD motifs of Pikm-2 do not affect the ability to associate with the sensor NLR Pik-1 compared to wild-type Pikm-2.
source: Following protein extraction and immunoprecipitation of Pik-1, we found that these mutations do not affect the ability to associate with the sensor NLR Pik-1 compared to wild-type Pikm-2 (Figure 8)
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 8.

claim: The reduced cell death activity in the Pik-1 P-loop mutant did not correlate with alterations in the association to the helper NLR Pik-2.
source: Similarly, the reduced cell death activity in the Pik-1 P-loop mutant did not correlate with alterations in the association to the helper NLR Pik-2 (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Pre-activated Pik NLR pair association does not require functional NLRs and is independent of nucleotide binding.
source: These results imply that pre-activated Pik NLR pair association does not require functional NLRs and is independent of nucleotide binding.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that P-loop and MHD mutants still associate with their partners.

claim: Pikp-2 acted as a suppressor of autoimmune phenotypes triggered by Pikp-1/Pikm-2 as increasing concentrations of Pikp-2 lowered the constitutive cell death phenotype.
source: Interestingly, Pikp-2 acted as a suppressor of autoimmune phenotypes triggered by Pikp-1/Pikm-2 as increasing concentrations of Pikp-2 lowered the constitutive cell death phenotype (Figure 9A and B, Figure 9—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 9A and B.

claim: Pikp-1 displays preference to signal through coevolved Pikp-2 rather than Pikm-2.
source: This reduction in cell death was evident even in the lowest concentration of Pikp-2 (Figure 9A and B, Figure 9—source data 1), suggesting that Pikp-1 displays preference to signal through coevolved Pikp-2 rather than Pikm-2.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the competition assay results showing that low concentrations of Pikp-2 reduce autoimmune cell death.

claim: Increasing concentrations of Pikp-2 reduced the association of Pikp-1 to Pikm-2, outcompeting Pikm-2 from a heterocomplex with Pikp-1.
source: Nevertheless, Co-IP results depicted a preference in association of Pikp-1 to Pikp-2 over Pikm-2. Increasing concentrations of Pikp-2 reduced the association of Pikp-1 to Pikm-2, outcompeting Pikm-2 from a heterocomplex with Pikp-1 (Figure 9C).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 9C.

claim: Coevolved Pik NLRs display preference in association over non-coevolved NLRs.
source: Altogether, these data reveal that coevolved Pik NLRs display preference in association over non-coevolved NLRs.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the competition assay and co-immunoprecipitation results.

claim: Increasing concentrations of Pikp-2 significantly reduced the cell death phenotype triggered by the combination of Pikp-1 and Pikp-2 Asp230Glu.
source: The combination of Pikp-1 and Pikp-2 Asp230Glu led to a strong cell death in the absence of effector (Figure 5). However, increasing concentrations of Pikp-2 significantly reduced this phenotype (Figure 10, Figure 10—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 10.

claim: The Pik-2 Glu230 polymorphism may be related to the preferential association between sensor and helper NLRs.
source: This indicates that the Pik-2 Glu230 polymorphism may also be related to the preferential association between sensor and helper NLRs in addition to its role in specialization towards AVR-Pik effector response and autoimmunity.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the competition assay results with the Asp230Glu mutant.

claim: No reduction of cell death phenotypes was observed with increasing concentrations of Pikp-2 mutants in the P-loop (Lys217Arg) or MHD (Asp559Val) motifs.
source: Although Pik NLRs do not require a functional P-loop or MHD motif to form heterocomplexes (Figure 8), we did not observe reduction of cell death phenotypes with increasing concentrations of Pikp-2 mutants in the P-loop (Lys217Arg) or MHD (Asp559Val) motifs (Figure 11, Figure 11—source data 1, Figure 11—source data 2), even at the highest concentration.
evidence: The claim is supported by cell death assay data shown in Figure 11.

claim: The P-loop and MHD motifs are important for the preferential sensor/helper association observed in Pikp-1 and Pikp-2.
source: This indicates that the P-loop and MHD motifs are important for the preferential sensor/helper association observed in Pikp-1 and Pikp-2.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that P-loop and MHD mutants cannot suppress autoimmune cell death in competition assays.

claim: Changes in Pik-2 helper NLR association to sensor Pik-1 from a resting state into an activated complex require functional P-loop and MHD motifs.
source: Altogether, these results suggest that changes in Pik-2 helper NLR association to sensor Pik-1 from a resting state into an activated complex require functional P-loop and MHD motifs.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the competition assay results with P-loop and MHD mutants.

claim: Mismatched pairs of Pik-1 and Pik-2 display constitutive cell death when combined in the heterologous system Nicotiana benthamiana.
source: Indeed, mismatched pairs of Pik-1 and Pik-2 display constitutive cell death when combined in the heterologous system Nicotiana benthamiana, which is reminiscent of autoimmune phenotypes.
evidence: The claim is supported by cell death assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: A single amino acid polymorphism in the helper NLR Pik-2 underpins both allelic specialization and immune homeostasis.
source: We identified a single amino acid polymorphism in the helper NLR Pik-2 that underpins both allelic specialization and immune homeostasis.
evidence: The claim is supported by mutagenesis and cell death assay data throughout the manuscript.

claim: NLR pairs can undergo co-adaptation and functional specialization.
source: Altogether, these results demonstrate that NLR pairs can undergo co-adaptation and functional specialization, offering a molecular framework to understand how they evolve to respond to pathogen effectors while maintaining a tight regulation of immune responses.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from all the experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: Pikm originated in the Chinese Japonica cultivar Hokushi Tami.
source: Pikm originated in the Chinese Japonica cultivar Hokushi Tami (Kiyosawa, 1978)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kiyosawa, 1978.

claim: Pikp originated in the Indica cultivar Pusur in Pakistan.
source: while Pikp originated in the Indica cultivar Pusur in Pakistan (Kiyosawa, 1969).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kiyosawa, 1969.

claim: Pikm pair mediated a hierarchical cell death response in the order of AVR-PikD>AVR-PikE>AVR-PikA.
source: As previously reported, Pikm pair mediated a hierarchical cell death response in the order of AVR-PikD>AVR PikE>AVR PikA (De la Concepcion et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to De la Concepcion et al., 2018.

claim: Pikp and Pikm allelic pairs trigger a strong cell death response in N. benthamiana when co-expressed with rice blast effector AVR-PikD, but not in the absence of effector.
source: The Pikp and Pikm allelic pairs trigger a strong cell death response in N. benthamiana when co-expressed with rice blast effector AVR-PikD, but not in the absence of effector (De la Concepcion et al., 2018; Maqbool et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to De la Concepcion et al., 2018 and Maqbool et al., 2015.

claim: The genetic linkage of the Pik NLR pair is ancient.
source: Evolutionary analyses have shown that the genetic linkage of this NLR pair is ancient and revealed marked signatures of adaptive evolution in the integrated HMA domain of Pik-1 (Białas et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Białas et al., 2021.

claim: The integrated HMA domain of Pik-1 shows marked signatures of adaptive evolution.
source: Evolutionary analyses have shown that the genetic linkage of this NLR pair is ancient and revealed marked signatures of adaptive evolution in the integrated HMA domain of Pik-1 (Białas et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Białas et al., 2021.

claim: Pik-1 HMA domain is the most sequence-diverged domain in the Pik NLR pair.
source: As a consequence, Pik-1 HMA domain is the most sequence-diverged domain in the Pik NLR pair (Białas et al., 2021; Białas et al., 2018; Costanzo and Jia, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Białas et al., 2021, Białas et al., 2018, and Costanzo and Jia, 2010.

claim: Pik-2 acts as a helper NLR that is required for the activation of immune responses.
source: While Pik-1 acts as a sensor, Pik-2 acts as a helper NLR that is required for the activation of immune responses (Maqbool et al., 2015; Zdrzałek et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Maqbool et al., 2015 and Zdrzałek et al., 2020.

claim: NLRs act as nucleotide-operated switches, exchanging ADP for ATP upon recognition.
source: Upon recognition, NLRs act as nucleotide-operated switches, exchanging ADP for ATP (Bernoux et al., 2016; Tameling et al., 2002; Wang et al., 2019b; Williams et al., 2011)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bernoux et al., 2016, Tameling et al., 2002, Wang et al., 2019b, and Williams et al., 2011.

claim: NLRs oligomerize into supramolecular signalling platforms upon activation.
source: Upon recognition, NLRs act as nucleotide-operated switches, exchanging ADP for ATP (Bernoux et al., 2016; Tameling et al., 2002; Wang et al., 2019b; Williams et al., 2011), and oligomerize into supramolecular signalling platforms (Hu et al., 2015; Ma et al., 2020; Martin et al., 2020; Sharif et al., 2019; Tenthorey et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2019a; Zhang et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple studies on NLR oligomerization.

claim: NLR activation leads to immune responses, including programmed cell death, that restrict pathogen growth.
source: This leads to immune responses, including programmed cell death, that restrict pathogen growth.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about NLR function in plant immunity.

claim: NLRs form the most expanded and diversified protein family in plants.
source: NLRs form the most expanded and diversified protein family in plants (Meyers et al., 2003; Van de Weyer et al., 2019; Yue et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Meyers et al., 2003, Van de Weyer et al., 2019, and Yue et al., 2012.

claim: Around 450 NLR proteins from 31 genera of flowering plants have been functionally validated.
source: Since their discovery, plant NLRs have been heavily studied and around 450 NLR proteins from 31 genera of flowering plants have been functionally validated (Kourelis et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kourelis et al., 2021.

claim: Plant NLRs often function in genetically linked pairs.
source: Plant NLRs present multiple layers of complexity (Barragan and Weigel, 2021), often functioning in genetically linked pairs (Eitas and Dangl, 2010; Griebel et al., 2014)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Eitas and Dangl, 2010 and Griebel et al., 2014.

claim: In paired NLRs, some act as 'sensors' that detect pathogen effectors while others act as 'helpers' that amplify and propagate immune signalling.
source: In such cases, NLRs specialize their role in immune activation, acting as 'sensors' that detect pathogen effectors or as 'helpers' that amplify and propagate immune signalling (Adachi et al., 2019b; Jubic et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Adachi et al., 2019b and Jubic et al., 2019.

claim: Paired NLRs are prevalent in plant genomes.
source: Paired NLRs are prevalent in plant genomes (Stein et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2019c)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Stein et al., 2018 and Wang et al., 2019c.

claim: A subset of sensor NLRs harbour atypical domains integrated into their architecture.
source: Paired NLRs are prevalent in plant genomes (Stein et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2019c) with a subset of sensor NLRs harbouring atypical domains integrated into their architecture (Bailey et al., 2018; Kourelis et al., 2021; Kroj et al., 2016; Sarris et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bailey et al., 2018, Kourelis et al., 2021, Kroj et al., 2016, and Sarris et al., 2016.

claim: Integrated domains in NLRs can be derived from pathogen host targets that act as sensor domains by binding pathogen effectors.
source: These domains can be derived from pathogen host targets that act as sensor domains within NLRs by binding pathogen effectors (Białas et al., 2018; Cesari et al., 2014; Maidment et al., 2021; Oikawa et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Białas et al., 2018, Cesari et al., 2014, Maidment et al., 2021, and Oikawa et al., 2020.

claim: When mismatched NLRs are combined in the same individual through genetic crossing, constitutive immune activation can occur, leading to deleterious phenotypes including dwarfism, necrosis, and lethality.
source: When these mismatched NLRs are combined in the same individual through genetic crossing, constitutive immune activation can occur, leading to deleterious phenotypes including dwarfism, necrosis, and lethality (Bomblies et al., 2007; Chae et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bomblies et al., 2007 and Chae et al., 2014.

claim: Hybrid necrosis has important implications in agriculture.
source: These 'Dangerous Mix' phenotypes are known in plant breeding as hybrid necrosis and have important implications in agriculture (Caldwell and Compton, 1943; Calvo-Baltanás et al., 2020; Hermsen, 1963b; Hermsen, 1963a; Li and Weigel, 2021; Wan et al., 2021; Yamamoto et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple studies on hybrid necrosis in agriculture.

claim: In Arabidopsis, two genetically unlinked NLR proteins encoded on different chromosomes were shown to physically associate in the mixed immune background of hybrid plants, underpinning hybrid necrosis.
source: In Arabidopsis, two genetically unlinked NLR proteins encoded on different chromosomes were shown to physically associate in the mixed immune background of hybrid plants, underpinning hybrid necrosis (Tran et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Tran et al., 2017.

claim: Association between NLRs and alleles of non-NLR proteins derived from a different genetic background was shown to induce NLR activation and autoimmune phenotypes.
source: Similarly, association between NLRs and alleles of non-NLR proteins derived from a different genetic background was also shown to induce NLR activation and autoimmune phenotypes (Barragan et al., 2019; Li et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Barragan et al., 2019 and Li et al., 2020.

claim: The Pik NLR pair occurs as allelic series in both Japonica and Indica rice cultivars.
source: The Pik NLR pair occurs as allelic series in both Japonica and Indica rice cultivars (Chaipanya et al., 2017; Costanzo and Jia, 2010; Hua et al., 2012; Xu et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Chaipanya et al., 2017, Costanzo and Jia, 2010, Hua et al., 2012, and Xu et al., 2008.

claim: The AVR-Pik effectors are polymorphic and present signatures of selection.
source: The AVR-Pik effectors are also polymorphic and present signatures of selection (Bentham et al., 2021; Białas et al., 2018; Yoshida et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bentham et al., 2021, Białas et al., 2018, and Yoshida et al., 2009.

claim: Allelic Pik NLRs have differential recognition specificities for the AVR-Pik variants.
source: Allelic Pik NLRs have differential recognition specificities for the AVR-Pik variants (De la Concepcion et al., 2021; Kanzaki et al., 2012)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to De la Concepcion et al., 2021 and Kanzaki et al., 2012.

claim: Differential recognition specificity of allelic Pik NLRs is underpinned by differential effector binding to the Pik-1 HMA domain.
source: Allelic Pik NLRs have differential recognition specificities for the AVR-Pik variants (De la Concepcion et al., 2021; Kanzaki et al., 2012), which is underpinned by differential effector binding to the Pik-1 HMA domain (De la Concepcion et al., 2018; De la Concepcion et al., 2021; Maqbool et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to De la Concepcion et al., 2018, De la Concepcion et al., 2021, and Maqbool et al., 2015.

claim: Two allelic variants of Pik-1, Pikp-1 and Pikm-1, acquired high-affinity binding to the M. oryzae AVR-Pik effector through convergent evolution of their HMA domains.
source: Two allelic variants of Pik-1, Pikp-1 and Pikm-1, acquired high-affinity binding to the M. oryzae AVR-Pik effector through convergent evolution of their HMA domains (Białas et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Białas et al., 2021.

claim: Pikm-1 and Pikh-1 alleles have been shown to convergently evolve towards extended recognition specificity of AVR-Pik variants.
source: Additionally, Pikm-1 and Pikh-1 alleles have been shown to convergently evolve towards extended recognition specificity of AVR-Pik variants (De la Concepcion et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to De la Concepcion et al., 2021.

claim: Cell death responses mediated by Pik in N. benthamiana have been shown to correlate with immune responses in rice.

claim: Pik-1 and Pik-2 have been coevolving for a long time, potentially before providing resistance to the blast fungus.
